_strings.@@1b090f3f0709: Print only the form pages (not instructions), single-sided; attach state copies of W-2/1099.
_strings.@@21e77ca4cc05: Minnesota Child and Dependent Care Credit — MN taxpayers (Single, Head of Household, Qualifying Surviving Spouse, or Married Filing Jointly) who had earned income and paid someone (not a spouse, the qualifying child's parent, or a dependent) to care for a qualifying person (e.g., a child under 13 or a disabled dependent/spouse) so they could work or look for work. Also available to certain licensed family daycare operators caring for their own young child, and for a child born in 2023 even without actual expenses. Unlike the federal credit, the MN credit is refundable.
_strings.@@250c1db41950: Minnesota Working Family Credit (state Earned Income Tax Credit) — Full-year or part-year MN residents who earned income from a job or self-employment (mirrors federal EIC). Must not be claimed as a dependent; investment income must be under $11,000; if no qualifying children, you (or spouse) must be age 19-64 and have a U.S. main home for more than half of 2023. Not available to full-year nonresidents, those with a 2- or 10-year federal EIC ban, or (generally) Married Filing Separately. Combined with the Child Tax Credit and the Credit for Qualifying Older Children on Schedule M1CWFC.
_strings.@@32c8baa30551: Renter's Property Tax Refund (renter's credit / 'circuit-breaker') — MN renters who in 2023 lived in a building where property taxes were payable (or payments in lieu of property taxes were payable) and received a CRP (Certificate of Rent Paid) from their landlord. Not available to anyone who can be claimed as a dependent on someone else's 2023 federal return. For tax year 2023 this was claimed on a separate return (Form M1PR), not the M1 income tax return (it moved onto the income tax return starting in 2024).
_strings.@@4cf945d1e9e4: Credit amounts/limits are not independently verified: State credits were researched from the cited DOR sources and are not tax advice — confirm each amount and your eligibility at the cited source before claiming it.
_strings.@@4d42ad525021: Mailing address: Some state facts could not be independently re-confirmed — see the pack's `unverified` list; confirm at the cited DOR source before relying on a specific figure/address.
_strings.@@581810a2465f: Minnesota Child Tax Credit — Full-year or part-year MN residents with one or more qualifying children under age 18 at the end of 2023 (qualifying child determined on Schedule M1DQC). Same base eligibility as the Working Family Credit (not a dependent of another, investment income under $11,000, not a full-year nonresident, generally not Married Filing Separately). ITIN may be used if no SSN.
_strings.@@873de0498f6f: 2023 Minnesota Individual Income Tax Forms and Instructions (Form M1) — Line 1 = Federal Adjusted Gross Income; Line 2 additions from Schedule M1M; residency rules (domicile + 183-day); due date April 15, 2024; Schedule M1NR; treaty references favor taxpayer only
_strings.@@e019ddb96b57: K-12 Education Credit — MN parents/guardians who paid education-related expenses in 2023 for a qualifying child in grades K-12 (a qualifying child is the same as for the federal Earned Income Credit). Qualifying expenses include things like tutoring by a qualified instructor, instructional materials, and certain educational services (private/parochial school tuition does NOT qualify for the credit). Refundable, so it can produce a refund even with no tax liability.
_strings.@@eb71823a243b: Multi-state income allocation (which dollars belong to which state) is your and the user's judgment; this tool scopes the returns and supplies the rules/warnings, not the allocation.
_strings.@@ef8b6764c7bc: Treaty conformity — MN conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from MN income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the MN return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Minnesota's resident return (Form M1) starts from federal adjusted gross income: the 2023 M1 instructions for Line 1 state "Line 1—Federal Adjusted Gross Income. Enter your 2023 federal adjusted gross income from: Line 11 of Form 1040 or 1040-SR, or 1040-NR." Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and therefore flows through. The Minnesota additions schedules (Schedule M1M lines 1-9, and Schedule M1MB) contain NO line that adds back income exempt under a U.S. income tax treaty. The complete 2023 M1M additions list is: out-of-state municipal bond interest (line 1), out-of-state mutual fund tax-exempt dividends (line 2), expenses attributable to income not taxed by MN (line 3), capital gain portion of a lump-sum distribution (line 4), M1HOME first-time homebuyer addition (line 5), and 529 distributions used for K-12 tuition (line 6) — lines 7-9 are intentionally blank. The only treaty references in the MN M1 instructions are FAVORABLE to the taxpayer (a nonresident alien may claim the standard deduction if allowed by a U.S. income tax treaty). Because there is no treaty addback, treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed -> conforms.

citation.source: 2023 Minnesota Individual Income Tax Forms and Instructions (Form M1), Minnesota Department of Revenue — Tax Rate Schedules, p.32 (Single / Married filing jointly or qualifying widow(er) / Married filing separately / Head of household); 2023 Tax Tables pp.25-31 with mandate 'If line 9 of Form M1 is less than $90,000, you must use the tax table'; Standard Deduction Table for Line 4, p.13; Worksheets A & B for Line 4 - Standard Deduction Limitation, p.14; Worksheet for Line 5 - Dependent Exemptions ($4,800), p.14; Line 10 - Tax From Table, p.16; 2023 Form M1 lines 1-10

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form M1 line 10: "Tax from the table or schedules in the Form M1 instructions". Instructions, Line 10 — Tax From Table: "Using the amount on line 9, find the tax amount in the column under your filing status." Tax Rate Schedules, p.32: "You must use these schedules if line 9 of Form M1 is $90,000 or more... If line 9 of Form M1 is less than $90,000, you must use the tax table on pages 25 through 31." This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply Form M1 line 1 = federal adjusted gross income (federal Form 1040/1040-SR line 11), adjusted for Minnesota items if any apply: ADD M1 line 2 additions (Schedule M1M line 10 and Schedule M1MB line 9) and SUBTRACT M1 line 6 (state income tax refund from federal Schedule 1 line 1) and M1 line 7 subtractions (Schedule M1M line 35 and Schedule M1MB line 21). The op then subtracts the shipped per-status standard deduction (M1 line 4) and $4,800 per dependent (M1 line 5) to reach M1 line 9, Minnesota taxable income, to which the rate schedule applies. Pass exemptions_count = 0 (Minnesota has no taxpayer/spouse personal exemption) and dependents_count = number of dependents claimed on Schedule M1DQC. TAX TABLE MANDATE below $90,000: 'If line 9 of Form M1 is less than $90,000, you must use the tax table on pages 25 through 31' (2023 M1 instructions, p.32); the rate schedules are only for line 9 of $90,000 or more. The table is built on $100-band midpoints, so bracket math may differ by a few dollars within table bands — the filed form must use the table. (Spot-checked: table rows $89,900-$90,000 and $34,400-$34,500 match midpoint bracket math for all statuses.) Qualifying Surviving Spouse: the p.32 rate-schedule column is titled 'Married filing jointly or qualifying widow(er)' — QSS uses the MFJ schedule exactly as mapped here, and the QSS standard deduction ($27,650 with 0 age/blind boxes) equals MFJ. Minnesota has NO personal exemption for the taxpayer or spouse: Form M1 line 5 is for DEPENDENTS only ($4,800 per dependent from Schedule M1DQC). Callers must pass exemptions_count = 0 and put dependents in dependents_count. Dependent-exemption phase-out NOT modeled (Worksheet for Line 5, p.14): the $4,800-per-dependent total is reduced by 2% for each $2,500 ($1,250 MFS) that M1 line 1 AGI exceeds $220,650 Single / $275,800 Head of Household / $330,950 MFJ-or-Surviving-Spouse / $165,475 MFS, and is $0 once the excess is more than $122,500 ($61,250 MFS). Standard-deduction limitation NOT modeled (Worksheets A & B for Line 4, p.14): if M1 line 1 AGI exceeds $220,650 ($110,325 MFS), the deduction is reduced by the LESSER of 80% of the deduction or [3% of the excess over $220,650/$110,325 (capped: enter $84,320, or $42,160 MFS, if AGI exceeds $304,970/$152,485) + 10% of the excess over $304,970 ($152,485 MFS)]; if AGI exceeds $1,000,000, the deduction is 20% of the table amount (Worksheet B). Additional standard deduction for age 65+/blind NOT modeled (Standard Deduction Table for Line 4, p.13): +$1,850 per checked box for Single and Head of Household (up to 2 boxes); +$1,450 per checked box for Married Filing Jointly (up to 4), Married Filing Separately (up to 4), and Qualified Surviving Spouse (up to 2). Enter it on the form's line 4. Standard-deduction gates NOT modeled: Married Filing Separately gets NO standard deduction if the spouse claims itemized deductions ('Not allowed' row, p.13); nonresident aliens may claim it only if allowed by a U.S. income tax treaty; a filer claimable as another's dependent uses the Worksheet for Line 4 - Dependent Standard Deduction (greater of $1,200 or earned income + $350, capped at $13,825, plus age/blind additions) — itemizers use Schedule M1SA instead. Printed rate-schedule constants check: every '$X +' constant equals the exact cumulative sum of the prior brackets rounded to the cent (divergence at most $0.005), EXCEPT the Head of Household top-bracket constant, printed $17,033.72 vs $17,033.71 exact cumulative (+$0.01, from chaining the rounded $9,577.00 constant). Maximum divergence from pure marginal math: $0.01. NOT modeled — amounts added after line 10: Minnesota Alternative Minimum Tax (Schedule M1MT, M1 line 11; can apply even without federal AMT) and M1 line 14 other taxes (Schedule M1HOME first-time-homebuyer recapture, Schedule M1529 education-savings-account recapture, Schedule M1LS tax on lump-sum distributions). Part-year residents and nonresidents: tax is prorated by the Minnesota-source percentage on Schedule M1NR (M1 lines 13/13a/13b) — NOT modeled; this pack computes full-year-resident tax. M1 line 9 (Minnesota taxable income) = line 3 (federal AGI + line 2 additions) - line 4 (standard/itemized deduction) - line 5 (dependent exemptions) - line 6 (taxable state income tax refund) - line 7 (M1M/M1MB subtractions). If additions, subtractions, or a taxable state refund apply, adjust the supplied taxable_base per base_guidance. Rounding: the M1 instructions say 'Round dollar amounts to the nearest whole dollar' (p.11 Reminders); the engine's round-half-up to whole dollars matches.
